purpose: One acquisition order per standard hull: which official file satisfies the anchor, which geometry route consumes it, under which licence, and under which digest. The plan exists so the remaining blocker is a named, single-valued fact (a URL and a sha256) rather than a paragraph saying 'official geometry is unavailable'.
url_null_policy: url is null for the entries that were not retrieved: a deep link written from memory would be a fabricated citation that the first real fetch would have to disprove. The custodian supplies it on the command line (--url SHIP=URL) and the value lands in the evidence with retrieval=network_fetch.
sha256_null_policy: sha256 is null where no bytes have been read in this environment, because no digest exists to pin. A payload read without a pin is refused (UnpinnedDigest) rather than praised as verified -- the digest of the first read is printed so the custodian can pin it.
pin_basis_note: Where a digest IS pinned below (KCS, KVLCC2), the pin basis is 'first_retrieval': the digest of the bytes as served by the publisher's portal on 2026-11-14. That is trust-on-first-use, not an independently published checksum -- it proves that a second retrieval returns the same file, not that the file is genuine. The HTTP response's own Last-Modified/ETag are recorded alongside so the retrieval can be replayed.

ships.locator: JBC (Japan Bulk Carrier) hull-surface geometry distributed with the Tokyo 2015 test case (Lpp 280.0 m, B 45.0 m, T 16.5 m, Cb 0.858)
ships.expected_file: the bulk-carrier hull surface, without the duct and rudder bulb (appendages are separate solids)
ships.notes: JBC's reference volume is currently a closure value (Cb*L*B*T), i.e. no external validation; the official file turns G7 into a real comparison. Appendages (duct, rudder bulb) would break the single-closed-shell gate, so the hull alone is ordered.

ships.locator: DTC (Duisburg Test Case) hull-surface geometry published by the University of Duisburg-Essen institute page (Lpp 355.0 m, B 51.0 m, T 14.5 m, Cb 0.661)
ships.expected_file: the post-panamax container-ship hull surface published with the DTC test case
ships.notes: The registry URL (https://www.uni-due.de/ship/dtc.php) answers HTTP 404 from this environment, so the portal has moved; the order stays open until a custodian supplies the current file URL rather than guessing one.

ships.locator: Todd's Series 60 parent-form offsets at L/B 7.5, B/T 2.5, Cb 0.60: stations x waterline half-breadths, as tabulated in the DTMB report
ships.expected_file: the parent-form offset table (stations x waterline half-breadths) digitised as CSV: header row of x/L values, one row per waterline, half-breadth in metres
ships.notes: The only genuinely public-domain source in the fleet. Offset tables go through the offset_table loft route, which closes the hull by construction (shared keel and deck vertices), so a table is enough to produce a watertight mesh.
